key_insight: Long-context decode reads only a few KV blocks per step, so per-block summary keys in DRAM can gate fetches and leave most KV on flash.
killer_doubt: Published since 2023-24. Flash bandwidth is the wall: top-32 64-token blocks x 80 layers is ~650 MB/step for 70B GQA, ~13 GB/s per stream at 20 tok/s (estimate).
decisive_experiment: None needed for novelty. Sizing only: run a ShadowKV/RetroInfer-style flash tier on Llama-3.1-70B over NVMe RAID; measure streams per SSD and RULER accuracy against block size and top-k. ~$30k.
prior_art: Landmark Attention (NeurIPS'23), Quest (ICML'24), InfLLM, ShadowKV, RetroInfer, InstInfer in-SSD attention [training knowledge]; R16 I-04022 and I-09974 dropped.

key_insight: Succinct structures lose to pointers on dependent cache misses, not on space. A controller-side rank/select/BP unit that fuses the 2-3 misses per hop could run ~2n-bit trees at pointer speed.
killer_doubt: Large read-mostly indexes are already compressed (Lucene FST/postings, delta CSR graphs, GBWT), so against today the footprint gain is ~1.5-2x on a few-percent share of DRAM (estimate).
decisive_experiment: Build an FPGA or CXL-expander rank/select/BP unit. Run a LOUDS trie, Elias-Fano graph BFS and FM-index on 50-100 GB datasets against SDSL on Xeon and pointer baselines; report ns/hop and bytes/node. ~$300k.
prior_art: SDSL/sux software rank/select, SWAR/BMI2 select; FM-index FPGA accelerators in genomics [training knowledge]. No general near-memory rank/select unit found (via search snippet).

key_insight: Profile-guided selection can find read-mostly maps, sets and trees whose information-theoretic size is far below their pointer size, then freeze them into succinct form.
killer_doubt: The compiler must prove immutability and keep iteration semantics. Most of the win sits in a few hand-tuned indexes, so automatic gain is likely <10% of heap (estimate).
decisive_experiment: Heap census of 20 production JVM/C++ services: measure the bytes in maps, sets and trees that are read-mostly after init, and their succinct size. Kill if that is <10% of heap. ~$50k.
prior_art: Automatic data-structure selection: Chameleon (PLDI'09), Brainy (PLDI'11), CollectionSwitch (CGO'18); succinct libraries SDSL, sux4j [training knowledge].

key_insight: Static-camera and screen streams repeat most patch tokens from frame to frame, so streaming VLM memory should scale with change, not with frame count.
killer_doubt: Dropping unchanged patches before the encoder saves KV and compute alike. A per-layer KV back-reference adds ~1.0-1.2x on top (estimate), and duplicated keys skew softmax mass.
decisive_experiment: On static-camera and screen-recording streams of about 1 hour, compare thresholded KV dedup against RLT-style input dropping and StreamingVLM at equal KV bytes; measure QA accuracy. ~$20k GPU.
prior_art: Eventful Transformers (ICCV'23) threshold-gated token updates; Run-Length Tokenization (NeurIPS'24); StreamingVLM, InfiniPot-V streaming KV compression [training knowledge].

key_insight: Ternary-trained models pack five trits per byte (3^5=243 states), 1.6 bpw, decoded by a 256-entry LUT on stock GPUs.
killer_doubt: Already shipped: llama.cpp TQ1_0 packs 5 trits per byte at ~1.69 bpw. Against today's 4-bit weights the gain is 2.5x, not 10x, and ternary quality at frontier scale is unproven.
decisive_experiment: None needed for novelty. Sizing only: compare a 7B BitNet-b1.58 model with a 4-bit GPTQ model of equal training compute on MMLU/GSM8K, and the HBM GB saved per served token. ~$150k compute.
prior_art: BitNet b1.58 (2024); llama.cpp TQ1_0/TQ2_0 ternary packing; bitnet.cpp and T-MAC LUT kernels [training knowledge].

key_insight: Adder-only units can skip zero weights in compute, which helps always-on edge accelerators save energy.
killer_doubt: BitNet zeros are ~1/3 and scattered, so ternary entropy is ~1.58 bits. Run-length coding saves ~0-6% beyond 5-trit packing and breaks random access (estimate).
decisive_experiment: None needed. Compute the empirical entropy and zero-run-length histogram of released BitNet-b1.58 weights; kill if RLE beats 1.6 bpw by <10%. ~$1k.
prior_art: Same mechanism as I-06286; BitNet b1.58, llama.cpp TQ1_0, TerEffic and sparse ternary kernels [training knowledge].

key_insight: Keep coarse codes in DRAM and put residual refinements on flash, fetched only on low confidence; this keeps ANN and embedding serving mostly out of DRAM.
killer_doubt: This is DiskANN (PQ codes in DRAM, full vectors on SSD for rerank), shipping since 2019. 32-64 B codes replace ~1.5-3 KB vectors, beating the claimed ~4x (estimate).
decisive_experiment: None needed for novelty. Sizing only: DiskANN versus a Matryoshka-style residual tier on a 1B-vector set; report DRAM GB and p99 latency at equal recall@10. ~$20k.
prior_art: DiskANN (NeurIPS'19), SPANN (NeurIPS'21), FAISS IVF-PQ with refine, Matryoshka embeddings (NeurIPS'22) [training knowledge].

key_insight: A 4 KB page compresses poorly alone; a shared per-workload trained dictionary supplies the context, plausibly lifting the ratio from 2x to 3x.
killer_doubt: Linux zram already accepts pre-trained zstd dictionaries. Going from 2x to 3x frees 1/6 of cold-tier bytes, ~3-8% of node DRAM at a 20-50% cold share (estimate).
decisive_experiment: Train per-class zstd dictionaries on 1 week of sampled fleet pages; replay zswap traces for JVM, Python and embedding services; report ratio and decompress latency with and without. ~$30k.
prior_art: zstd dictionary training; Linux zram algorithm_params pre-trained dictionaries (~6.12); Thesaurus (ASPLOS'20) cluster-base compression [training knowledge].

key_insight: The KV cache is a highly correlated tensor, so media-codec transform coding (decorrelate, adaptively quantize, entropy-code) beats per-element quantization for storage.
killer_doubt: KVTC (ICLR 2026) already does PCA transform, adaptive bit widths and entropy coding at up to 20x (via search snippet), beating the 4-8x claim. RoPE breaks token-axis smoothness of keys.
decisive_experiment: Add a token-axis DCT (values, pre-RoPE keys) on top of a KVTC-style channel PCA. Measure the extra compression at equal RULER/LongBench accuracy on Llama-3.1-8B; kill if <1.3x. ~$20k.
prior_art: KVTC, Staniszewski & Lancucki (arXiv 2511.01815, ICLR 2026) (via search snippet); KIVI, KVQuant, GEAR, Palu low-rank KV [training knowledge].

key_insight: Frozen weights need no endurance or refresh, and one via mask on a generic base array is the cheapest per-model customisation of storage.
killer_doubt: HBF claims 8-16x HBM capacity at similar cost (via search snippet), against ~3x cheaper for via-ROM, so HBF wins ~3-5x on $/GB and is rewritable; models churn every 3-6 months.
decisive_experiment: None needed for novelty. Sizing only: a $/GB and latency model of a 28 nm via-ROM base-die stack versus HBF for MoE random-expert access, using the published HBF spec. ~$20k.
prior_art: Taalas HC1 mask-ROM weights on N6, AMD acquiring (via R16 snippet); SanDisk/SK hynix HBF OCP spec (Aug 2026); YOLoC ROM-CiM; R16 family I-02186/I-01226.

key_insight: In large-batch decode every replica consumes the identical weight stream, so one copy can be multicast to many accelerators instead of being stored N times.
killer_doubt: Each receiver still needs full weight bandwidth: 70 GB FP8 at 20 steps/s is 1.4 TB/s (~11 Tb/s) optical input per accelerator. Wide TP/EP already stores weights ~once per rack.
decisive_experiment: Trace a 72-GPU wide-EP deployment and a DP-replica deployment for duplicated weight GB per rack; emulate the carousel phase-alignment latency with NCCL multicast on 8 GPUs. ~$50k.
prior_art: Cerebras MemoryX/SwarmX weight streaming; Fiber Memory preprint arXiv 2607.08407 (via R16 snippet); NVLink SHARP multicast; R16 I-00277 dropped, I-05406 HOLD.

key_insight: The same bytes often sit in page cache, socket buffers, heap and GPU staging; a content-hash census turns zero-copy work into a ranked, measurable hit list.
killer_doubt: In-flight copies are transient and small. KSM, O_DIRECT and io_uring already cover the persistent cases, so fleet savings are likely ~2-5%, not 10-25% (estimate).
decisive_experiment: Run the eBPF plus sampled page-hash census on 50 storage, proxy and ingest nodes for 2 weeks; report time-averaged duplicate bytes as % of RSS. Kill if <5%. ~$40k.
prior_art: Linux KSM page-hash merging; Meta TMO fleet memory work; io_uring registered buffers, MSG_ZEROCOPY, splice [training knowledge].
